summary: whalibmob 5.33.28: unverified network and filesystem patterns in library modules
details: The package ships several modules combining filesystem reads, HTTPS/HTTP requests, and shell-related tokens: lib/MediaService.js imports fs, http, and https and performs fs.readFileSync and https.request calls; lib/Registration.js contains repeated references to 'ping'; lib/WebVersion.js references 'curl', 'ps', and https.get; lib/socks.js references 'curl', 'POST', and 'hostname'. The package name resembles a well-known library family, and the module names (MediaService, Registration, WebVersion, socks) do not match any documented purpose that was identified. The co-occurrence of network, filesystem, and process primitives in multiple files is consistent with both legitimate library composition and exfiltration tooling; no specific installer-side data read or non-first-party destination was identified in the available evidence, so the pattern-match alone does not establish an attacker-benefit flow.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
